questions_for_hospital: Has anyone observed her setting up and taking her own medications (for example with a pill box) since the delirium improved? Could OT or nursing document this before discharge?
What was her orientation on the most recent assessments? The notes show AOx3 on 10/04, AOx4 on 10/05 and disorientation overnight 10/05-10/06.
Could OT assess showering and toileting hygiene before discharge?
Is she on any isolation precautions?
Can you send the CalAIM authorization once the plan responds?
Will she leave with a 30-day supply of her medications?

claude_fit.reason: Mobility and infection are fine (MOB-3 met with walker, GU-E1 UTI on oral antibiotics, INF-1 and INF-2 negative), but orientation flips between AOx3 and AOx4 with nighttime disorientation (COG-2 unknown) and nobody documents that she can self-administer meds despite needing reminders (COG-1 unknown). Ask for a med-management check, a current orientation assessment and shower/toileting (ADL-2, ADL-3) before deciding.
